what: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners owns essential infrastructure worldwide: regulated utilities, toll roads and rail, gas pipelines and processing, and data centres and towers. It is managed by Brookfield and structured as a partnership.
customers: Shippers, utilities, telecom operators and industrial users who pay to use its networks under regulated or contracted terms.
money: rail, toll roads, ports and terminals
moat: Assets that are regulated monopolies or have contracts running for decades, in businesses where no one would build a second network alongside.
risks: Consolidated debt of about $61 billion, though most is non-recourse at the asset level
Rising interest rates raise financing costs for an asset-heavy business
It is a partnership, which complicates tax reporting for some investors
Reported net margin is low because of depreciation and minority interests
opportunities: Revenue grew about 10% last year and about 17% a year over three years
Most revenue is regulated or contracted and linked to inflation
A distribution yield above 4% with a record of annual increases
watch: Funds from operations per unit and the pace of asset sales funding new investments.
